images.note: Contemporary front page, New-York Tribune, May 8, 1915 (day after the sinking). Banner headline '1,300 Die as Lusitania Goes to Bottom; 400 Americans on Board Torpedoed Ship; Washington Stirred as When Maine Sank' with a photo of the Lusitania. Covers the script's Box 2 beat: May 7, 1915 torpedoing, 128 Americans dead. Source scan 6224x8334; served at 3000px wide via IIIF. alt_url null: no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px Lusitania image (LOC photo derivatives cap at 640px; IWM photos cap at 800px; IWM 'Remember the Lusitania' poster 556x800).
images.title: Lusitania sunk — New-York Tribune front page, May 8, 1915

images.note: Contemporary front page, New-York Tribune, November 10, 1916. Headline 'Wilson Re-elected with 272 Votes; California Gives Him 3,000 Plurality.' Covers the script beat: Wilson ran on 'He kept us out of war' and won by a whisker, California deciding it. (The Nov 8 edition prematurely called it for Hughes and was rejected as beat-mismatched.) Source scan 6205x8414; served at 3000px wide via IIIF. alt_url null: no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px 1916-campaign image (no 'He kept us out of war' poster found digitized at LOC).
images.title: Wilson re-elected — New-York Tribune front page, November 10, 1916

images.note: Contemporary front page, New-York Tribune, February 1, 1917 (day after Berlin's announcement). Banner 'Berlin Orders Ruthless U-Boat War; Puts Rigid Limit on American Ships; Washington Fears Break Will Follow' plus the full 'TEXT OF GERMAN WARNING.' Covers the script's Box 3 beat: Jan 31, 1917 resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare; Wilson broke relations three days later. Source scan 6317x8447; served at 3000px wide via IIIF. alt_url null: no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px WWI U-boat photo (IWM photos cap at 800px; LOC Bain/Harris&Ewing derivatives cap at 640px).
images.title: Unrestricted U-boat warfare announced — New-York Tribune front page, February 1, 1917

images.note: Contemporary front page, New-York Tribune, March 1, 1917. Banner 'Germany Asks Mexico To Seek Alliance with Japan for War on U.S.' with subhead on Zimmermann's message to Carranza promising Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, plus the full printed text under 'ZIMMERMANN'S INSTRUCTIONS.' Covers the script's Box 3 beat exactly as Americans read it the morning of March 1. Source scan 6322x8535; served at 3000px wide via IIIF; headline visually confirmed. alt_url null: the coded original is held by NARA but the NARA catalog API served only its JS shell (no media URLs retrievable), and no other institution offered a verifiable >=1200px image of the telegram document.
images.title: Zimmermann telegram published — New-York Tribune front page, March 1, 1917

images.note: Contemporary front page, New-York Tribune, April 3, 1917 (morning after the address). Headlines 'The President Calls for War Without Hate' and 'Wilson's Plan Provides for Full Warfare,' reporting Wilson's April 2 joint-session address asking Congress for war ('the world must be made safe for democracy'; declaration followed April 6). Covers the script's climax beat. Source scan 6254x8389; served at 3000px wide via IIIF; headline visually confirmed. alt_url null: the famous Harris & Ewing photo of Wilson addressing Congress (LOC) is only served at 640px; no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px image.
images.title: Wilson asks Congress for war — New-York Tribune front page, April 3, 1917
